'''Giorgio Benedek''' (born 4 February 1941) is an Italian physicist, academic and researcher. He is an emeritus Professor of Physics of Matter at [[University of Milano-Bicocca]]<ref name=UNIM>{{Cite web|url=https://www.unimib.it/giorgio-benedek|title=BENEDEK GIORGIO|website=Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca}}</ref> and Director of the International School of Solid State Physics at [[Ettore Majorana Foundation and Centre for Scientific Culture]].<ref name="EMFCSC">{{Cite web|url=http://www.emfcsc.infn.it/em/schools/index.html|title=EMFCSC|website=www.emfcsc.infn.it}}</ref>

Benedek's original theoretical interest in the dynamics and vibrational response functions of defects in solids has been extended to various research areas regarding low-dimensional systems, like surface dynamics and surface phonon spectroscopy, the topology and physics of cluster-assembled carbon, and the physics of [[Helium|He]] quantum droplets and solids.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=bbolHoMAAAAJ&hl=it|title=Giorgio Benedek|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

Benedek is emeritus foreign member of the [[Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium|Royal Academy of Belgium]], member of the [[Istituto Lombardo Accademia di Scienze e Lettere|Istituto Lombardo – Accademia di Scienze e Lettere]], of the Istituto di Studi Superiori Gerolamo Cardano, a fellow of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts|European Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.unimib.it/news/prof-giorgio-benedek-nominato-fellow-delleuropean-academy-sciences|title=Il prof. Giorgio Benedek nominato Fellow dell'European Academy of Sciences|date=October 20, 2020|website=Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca}}</ref> of the [[European Physical Society]], and of the [[Italian Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.sif.it/news/29|title=EPS Fellows}}</ref>

== Career ==
Benedek studied at the [[University of Milano]] and received his Doctoral degree in physics, and his University Teaching Qualification in Solid State Physics in 1965 and 1970, respectively. Benedek worked at the [[Joint Research Centre]] (JRC) in [[Ispra]] before being appointed for a permanent research position at [[National Research Council (Italy)|Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche]] (CNR) from 1967 till 1984. This appointment allowed him to teach at the University of Milano as a lecturer of Physics for Biological Sciences from 1970 till 1984. In the following year, he was promoted to associate professor, then in 1986 Full Professor of Structure of Matter. In this position he moved in 1998 to the Department of Materials Science of the University of Milano-Bicocca. Benedek was appointed as an emeritus Professor of Physics of Matter at this university after his retirement in 2011.<ref name=UNIM/><ref name=IOP>{{cite journal |last1=Giessibl |first1=Franz J |last2=Morita |first2=Seizo |last3=Morita |first3=Seizo |title=Giorgio Benedek: an extraordinary universal scientist |journal=Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter |date=14 March 2012 |volume=24 |issue=10 |article-number=100401 |doi=10.1088/0953-8984/24/10/100401 |pmid=22354819 }}</ref>

Benedek has been a regular visiting scientist at the [[Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research|Max-Planck Institut (MPI) für Festkörperforschung]], Stuttgart (1978–1987), the MPI für Strömungsforschung (now Dynamik und Selbstorganisation) in Göttingen, Germany, since 1980, and at Donostia International Physics Center (DIPC) since 2003. He directs the International School of Solid State Physics since 1990, and is a co-director of the International School of Complexity at the Ettore Majorana Foundation and Centre for Scientific Culture<ref name="EMFCSC"/> in Sicily, Italy. Benedek has also held in his career numerous administrative positions.<ref name=IOP/>

== Research ==
In the 1970s, Benedek transferred the Green's function methods, originally applied to the dynamics and the vibrational response functions of defects in solids, to the theory of surface phonons and inelastic atom surface scattering. By applying the atom-surface scattering theory of Vittorio Celli, [[Nicolás Cabrera (physicist)|Nicolás Cabrera]] and Dick Manson, Benedek predicted the feasibility of surface-phonon spectroscopy with inelastic Helium atom scattering (HAS).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Benedek |first1=Giorgio |last2=Toennies |first2=J.Peter |title=Helium atom scattering spectroscopy of surface phonons: genesis and achievements |journal=Surface Science |date=January 1994 |volume=299-300 |pages=587–611 |doi=10.1016/0039-6028(94)90683-1 |bibcode=1994SurSc.299..587B }}</ref>

The collaboration of Benedek with [[Jan Peter Toennies]] led to a full development of HAS surface phonon spectroscopy for different classes of materials. Within this collaboration, Benedek and coworkers predicted or explained several inelastic HAS effects like the kinematical focusing, the anomalous longitudinal resonance, the inelastic bound-state resonance-enhancement and the quantum sonar effect, by which HAS from a conducting surface can detect deep subsurface phonons via the electron-phonon interaction.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ernst |first1=Wolfgang E. |title=Atomic Scale Dynamics at Surfaces: Theory and Experimental Studies with Helium Atom Scattering Giorgio Benedek and J. Peter Toennies, Springer, New York, NY, 2018. 652 pp. {{text|ISBN}}: 3662564416. |journal=Microscopy and Microanalysis |date=February 2020 |volume=26 |issue=1 |page=182 |doi=10.1017/S1431927619015265 |bibcode=2020MiMic..26..182E |s2cid=213064668 }}</ref>

Benedek with Chakram S. Jayanthi, Winfried Kress and Heinz Bilz developed the multipole-expansion model (also termed pseudo-charge model) for the analysis of surface dynamics and inelastic HAS spectra. In the same group at the MPI-FKF in Stuttgart, Benedek joined Bilz and Annette Bussmann-Holder in a series of papers presenting a new nonlinear electron-phonon theory of ferroelectricity.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Statics and Dynamics of Nonlinear Systems|editor-first1=Giorgio|editor-last1=Benedek|editor-first2=Heinz|editor-last2=Bilz|editor-first3=Roland|editor-last3=Zeyher|date=January 8, 1983|series=Springer Series in Solid-State Sciences|volume=47|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-82135-6|isbn=978-3-642-82137-0}}{{page needed|date=July 2021}}</ref> [[K. Alex Müller|Karl-Alex Müller]] and Benedek started in 1989 a periodic series of Erice workshops on high-temperature superconductivity.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ilnuovosaggiatore.sif.it/download/58|title=Il Nuovo Saggiatore Bollettino Della Società Italiana Di Fisica}}</ref>

In late 90s, Benedek and his group in Milano predicted by quantum simulations various forms of carbon cluster-assembled materials like clathrates and schwarzites. Soon after, Paolo Milani and coworkers, in collaboration with Benedek's group, produced carbon schwarzites, thus synthesizing the 3D sp2 carbon allotrope, after 0D fullerenes, 1D nanotubes, and 2D graphene.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9780792370413|title=Nanostructured Carbon for Advanced Applications: Proceedings of the NATO Advanced Study Institute on Nanostructured Carbon for Advanced Applications Erice, Sicily, Italy July 19–31, 2000|series=NATO Science Series II: Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry|editor-first1=Giorgio|editor-last1=Benedek|editor-first2=P.|editor-last2=Milani|editor-first3=V. G.|editor-last3=Ralchenko|date=January 8, 2001|publisher=Springer Netherlands|doi=10.1007/978-94-010-0858-7|isbn=978-0-7923-7042-0|via=www.springer.com}}{{page needed|date=July 2021}}</ref>

Benedek in a 1996 work with Toennies, Andrey Vilesov and other colleagues formulated a vibronic theory of a molecule trapped in a 4He droplet that confirmed the droplet superfluidity. More recently his analysis of the geyser effect observed by Toennies in vacuum expansion from a 4He solid provided evidence of condensation of excess vacancies causing a superfluid flow of solid 4He.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Benedek |first1=Giorgio |last2=Dalfovo |first2=Franco |last3=Grisenti |first3=Robert E. |last4=Käsz |first4=Manuel |last5=Toennies |first5=J. Peter |title=Oscillations in the Expansion of Solid He 4 into Vacuum |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=26 August 2005 |volume=95 |issue=9 |article-number=095301 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.095301 |pmid=16197222 |bibcode=2005PhRvL..95i5301B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Benedek |first1=Giorgio |last2=Kalinin |first2=Anton |last3=Nieto |first3=Pablo |last4=Toennies |first4=J. Peter |title=Vacancy-induced flow of solid helium |journal=Physical Review B |date=4 March 2016 |volume=93 |issue=10 |article-number=104505 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.93.104505 |bibcode=2016PhRvB..93j4505B }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* 1985 - International Francqui Chair
* 1990 - Alexander von Humboldt Forschungspreis
* 1992 - Co-recipient of the Max Planck Prize with Jan Peter Toennies
* 2000 - Foreign Member of the Royal Academy of Belgium 
* 2009 - Fellow of the Italian Physical Society 
* 2010 - Effective Member of the Istituto Lombardo Accademia di Scienze e Lettere<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.istitutolombardo.it/pdf/elencosoci2018.pdf|title=Elenco Completo Membri e Soci|access-date=2020-12-29|archive-date=2021-01-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125073401/http://www.istitutolombardo.it/pdf/elencosoci2018.pdf}}</ref>
* 2010 - Fellow of the European Physical Society<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eps.org/page/distinction_fellows|title=EPS Fellows}}</ref>
* 2014 - Volta Medal, [[University of Pavia]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gssi.it/communication/news-events/item/2041-medaglia-voltiana-assegnata-a-eugenio-coccia|title=Medaglia Voltiana assegnata a Eugenio Coccia|website=www.gssi.it}}</ref>
* 2014 - International Prize for Physics of the National Academy of Lincei
* 2016 - Honorary Member of Centro Fermi in Rome
* 2018 - European Physical Society Achievement Award<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eps.org/page/distinction_prize_AA|title=EPS Achievement Award}}</ref>
* 2020 - Fellow of the European Academy of Sciences<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurasc.org/user/793/giorgio-benedek|title=European Academy of Sciences - Giorgio Benedek|website=www.eurasc.org}}</ref>
* 2022 - Co-recipient of the Enrico Fermi Prize of the Italian Physical Society with Jan Peter Toennies<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sif.it/media/5d358dd.pdf|title=The Fermi prize 2022 of the Italian Physical Society to Solid State Physics}}</ref>
